statements: Create recurrence.mjs at the workspace root: an ES module with one named function export, nextOccurrences(rule, afterDate, count). Use Node.js built-ins only and no dependencies. Tests, if you write any, go under test/. Dates are ISO strings YYYY-MM-DD in the Gregorian calendar; no clocks, no time zones.

rule is an object with freq ('monthly' or 'yearly'), interval (integer 1..120), start (a date), exactly one of byDay (an object with nth, an integer -5..5 but not 0, and weekday, an integer 0..6) or byMonthDay (an integer -31..31 but not 0), and optional onMissing ('skip' or 'clamp') and exceptions (an array of dates). afterDate is a date and count an integer 0..60.

A date is a real date written exactly YYYY-MM-DD, year 1900..2200. A wrong type (dates, freq and onMissing are strings; the numbers are finite numbers; rule and byDay are plain objects; exceptions is an array) throws a TypeError, code 'E_TYPE'. Right type but invalid value, or both or neither of byDay and byMonthDay, throws a RangeError, code 'E_RANGE'. Type checks run before any range check.

Time is cut into periods 0, 1, 2 and so on. Monthly: period k is the month that is k times interval months after the month of start. Yearly: period k is the month of start in the year that is k times interval years after the year of start. Periods are counted from start, never from afterDate. Each period yields at most one date; a period that yields none still counts.

byMonthDay of 5 means the 5th day of the period's month; a negative value counts from the end, so -1 is the last day and -2 the day before it. byDay means the nth day of the month that falls on weekday, nth counted from the first of the month, or from the end when negative (-1 is the last such day). Weekday 0 is Monday, 1 is Tuesday, up to 6 for Sunday.

When the requested day does not exist in that month (day 30 in February, a 5th Friday, -5 Sunday), onMissing decides, and it defaults to 'skip': the period yields no date. With 'clamp' the period yields the existing day nearest the requested position: the last matching day when the request counted from the start, the first matching day when it counted from the end.

The result lists, in ascending order, the first count dates that are strictly after afterDate, not before start, and not in exceptions. A date in exceptions is dropped and does not count toward count. Dates after 2200-12-31 are never produced, so the result can be shorter than count, or empty.
The function is pure: no I/O, no shared state, the arguments are not mutated, and a new array is returned.
brief: Implement recurrence.mjs exactly as the numbered statements specify, then stop. Do not change any other file except tests under test/.
